title: A final delivery must expose one machine-readable current-state authority and retire stale authorities
trigger: One delivered archive contains multiple manifest-pinned receipts or top-level manifests that make opposite claims about whether the same revision is installed, run, or current, without an explicit machine-readable authority and supersession relation.

currentReplay.subject: A4_ORIGINAL_NOSE_R02_INSTALLED_ISSUE.zip
currentReplay.observation: ENTRY_SHA_MANIFEST.json verifies 4020/4020 and pins ORIGINAL_REBUILD_CURRENT.json as installed inspection ISSUE, INSTALL_RECEIPT.json as INSTALLED_NOT_YET_GLES_VERIFIED, NOSE_R02_INSPECTION_GLES_QA.json as ACTUAL_GLES3_LOCAL_ASSEMBLY, and FINAL_STATUS.json as FROZEN_PREPARED_NOT_INSTALLED with installed=NO, installer=NOT_EXECUTED and actualGPU=NOT_RUN. The same archive also exposes a top-level FINAL_ENTRY_SHA_MANIFEST.json with 130 hash mismatches, including an older ORIGINAL_REBUILD_CURRENT.json identity, and neither top-level manifest declares authority precedence or supersession.

noveltyAgainstExistingCases.CANDIDATE_ATOMIC_EVIDENCE_COMMIT_001: Different failure: no concurrent mutation or validation-to-publication race is needed; the immutable delivered bytes themselves expose opposite current-state authorities.
noveltyAgainstExistingCases.CANDIDATE_EXECUTABLE_RESOURCE_CLOSURE_00: Different failure: the relevant receipts and manifests are present and executable evidence exists; the missing property is unique state authority and explicit supersession, not resource closure.
noveltyAgainstExistingCases.TERRAIN_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_001: Same broad no-stale principle, but this replay adds a cross-receipt and cross-manifest machine rule for one archive and is kept Candidate rather than changing the production regression globally.

candidateRule.verifierGate: Fail closed unless exactly one machine-readable current-state authority is named; every top-level manifest either verifies against delivered bytes or is explicitly marked superseded/non-authoritative; every non-history receipt about the same revision agrees on installed/run/current semantics. Historical receipts may remain only under declared history with a machine-readable supersededBy relation.

minimumFalsifiableTrial.scope: one A4 Nose R02 ISSUE delivery copy
minimumFalsifiableTrial.pass: A consumer starting only from the archive root resolves exactly one current-state authority; its SHA verifies; all top-level manifests verify or are explicitly superseded; querying installed/run/current yields one answer while INSPECTION_ISSUE_NOT_ACCEPTED remains unchanged.
minimumFalsifiableTrial.fail: Two root-reachable authoritative paths still yield opposite installed/run/current answers, or a top-level manifest fails its own hashes without an explicit superseded/non-authoritative state.

boundaries: This case does not reject the actual GLES installation evidence or the 147-program/1320-draw bounded assembly.
This case does not promote Nose R02 shape, interface, motion, whole-train, production, or user acceptance; INSPECTION_ISSUE_NOT_ACCEPTED remains authoritative content.
Historical pre-install evidence may remain if it is moved or classified as history and linked by supersededBy.
Candidate is not globally adopted until a single-Mother repaired delivery passes the same root-only consumer replay.
rollback: Retire this Candidate if the archive already contains a documented machine-readable precedence/supersession rule that deterministically makes the stale manifest and pre-install FINAL_STATUS non-authoritative for every root-only consumer.
